# tritonctl firewall-rule

Manage firewall rules

Alias: fwrule

Subcommands: list, show, create, update, delete

Usage: `tritonctl firewall-rule [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>`

## tritonctl firewall-rule list

List firewall rules in the project, or on one VPC

Alias: ls

Usage: `tritonctl firewall-rule list [OPTIONS]`

- `--vpc <VPC>`: Only the rules of this VPC (name, uuid, or prefix)

## tritonctl firewall-rule show

Show one firewall rule

Usage: `tritonctl firewall-rule show [OPTIONS] <ID>`

- `<ID>`: Rule name, uuid, or prefix

## tritonctl firewall-rule create

Create a firewall rule on a VPC

Usage: `tritonctl firewall-rule create [OPTIONS] --vpc <VPC> --name <NAME> --action <ACTION> --direction <DIRECTION> --priority <PRIORITY>`

- `--vpc <VPC>`: VPC the rule applies to (name, uuid, or prefix) (required)
- `--name <NAME>` (required)
- `--description <DESCRIPTION>`
- `--action <ACTION>` (required; one of: allow, deny)
- `--direction <DIRECTION>` (required; one of: inbound, outbound)
- `--protocol <PROTOCOL>` (one of: any, tcp, udp, icmp4, icmp6; default: any)
- `--priority <PRIORITY>` (required)
- `--source-cidr <SOURCE_CIDR>`: Source CIDR (optional; omitted means any)
- `--destination-cidr <DESTINATION_CIDR>`: Destination CIDR (optional; omitted means any)
- `--source-ports <SOURCE_PORTS>`: Source ports as `low-high` or one port (TCP/UDP only)
- `--destination-ports <DESTINATION_PORTS>`: Destination ports as `low-high` or one port (TCP/UDP only)

## tritonctl firewall-rule update

Change a firewall rule. Only the flags given change

Usage: `tritonctl firewall-rule update [OPTIONS] <ID>`

- `<ID>`: Rule name, uuid, or prefix
- `--name <NAME>`
- `--description <DESCRIPTION>`
- `--action <ACTION>` (one of: allow, deny)
- `--direction <DIRECTION>` (one of: inbound, outbound)
- `--protocol <PROTOCOL>` (one of: any, tcp, udp, icmp4, icmp6)
- `--priority <PRIORITY>`
- `--enable`: Turn the rule on
- `--disable`: Turn the rule off without deleting it
- `--source-cidr <SOURCE_CIDR>`
- `--destination-cidr <DESTINATION_CIDR>`
- `--source-ports <SOURCE_PORTS>`: Source ports as `low-high` or one port
- `--destination-ports <DESTINATION_PORTS>`: Destination ports as `low-high` or one port

## tritonctl firewall-rule delete

Delete a firewall rule

Alias: rm

Usage: `tritonctl firewall-rule delete [OPTIONS] <ID>`

- `<ID>`: Rule name, uuid, or prefix
- `-n, --dry-run`: Print what would change and stop
- `-y, --yes`: Answer yes to the confirmation. The summary still prints
- `--keep-going`: Keep executing after a step fails
